subject: Concurrency & rate limit follow-up — Cardinal Labs pilot
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Cardinal pilot — concurrency & streaming clarifications

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we promised to follow up on so your infra and engineering teams can sign off: 

1) Workload profile (what you told us)
- Peak parallel inference calls: ~200 simultaneous short-response requests (avg 8-12 tokens per response)
- Streaming sessions (long-lived): ~75 concurrent streams delivering chunked partial responses, typical session length 30–90s
- Burst requirement: ability to absorb 3x baseline for short windows (~60–90s) during batch imports
- Latency target: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms for the short-response path (95th mostly network + inference)

2) Redwood ask / clarifying questions
- Confirm whether streaming sessions require independent socket allotment vs multiplexing over fewer sockets
- Confirmation of acceptable throttling behavior (graceful 429 vs queued tokens)
- Pilot duration target: 6 weeks with a ramp to the concurrent levels above within 2 weeks

3) Next steps (who does what)
- Redwood (Ben + Grace): propose a connection/concurrency matrix and a temporary ratecap proposal for the pilot by EOD tomorrow. Attachment: cardinal_conn_requirements.xlsx (we'll populate with our assumptions).
- Cardinal (Alex / Priya): share firewall egress IPs, expected region for deployment (we noted us-west), and any existing WebSocket gateway constraints.

If anything in the recap is off, flag it and we will adjust. Ben and Grace — copying you for the matrix + ratecard draft.

Thanks,
Neha

Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment(s): cardinal_conn_requirements.xlsx (stub)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cardinallabs.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cardinal pilot — concurrency & streaming clarifications

Thanks Neha — that summary is accurate. A couple notes from our infra side: 

- We can provision for 200 short-response concurrent requests as a starting point. Our preference is to keep streaming sessions on a separate pool so we can monitor resource usage — so yes, independent allotment makes sense.
- Firewall / egress IPs: 52.23.120.5, 52.23.120.6 (we'll confirm the CIDR tomorrow).
- We want to avoid sudden 429s for production traffic — can you outline how Redwood handles backpressure? Ideally we hit a queued/slowdown behavior before hard rejects for streaming sessions.

Also, one ask: can Redwood provide an explicit temporary quota for sockets (connection pool) and parallel request slots during the pilot so our SREs can simulate load without being rate limited by the live tier?

Alex

Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering | Cardinal Labs
alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0138

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 11:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cardinal pilot — concurrency & streaming clarifications

Alex — appreciate the detail. Quick answers and an initial proposal attached (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) plus the filled matrix in the shared sheet. Highlights: 

- Backpressure model: by default Redwood will attempt graceful degradation: short-response path uses adaptive batching + token-level queuing for a 10s window before returning a 429. Streaming sessions are kept on a separate pool; when stream capacity reaches the soft limit we surface a 503-overload with a Retry-After header rather than abrupt socket drops. For pilot we can enable a "gentle-queue" mode where short blocks are buffered for up to 5s then retried.

- Temporary pilot quotas (proposed):
  * Connection pool (socket handles): 500
  * Parallel short-response slots: 220 guaranteed, 300 burst available for 90s windows (subject to resource availability)
  * Streaming sessions: 100 concurrent streams (isolated pool)
  * Burst tokens: 3x baseline for 60s, 1.5x for 10m rolling window

- Latency SLOs we can target during pilot: p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 350ms for short responses in us-west region (measured inside Redwood endpoint). We'll instrument token-level tracing and per-route cost during the pilot so you get visibility.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (summary of pricing & pilot credits) ; cardinal_conn_requirements.xlsx (updated matrix).

If that aligns we can create the pilot quota record and provide an API key for load-tests.

—Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment(s): redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (stub), cardinal_conn_requirements.xlsx (stub)

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cardinallabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cardinal pilot — concurrency & streaming clarifications

Ben / Neha — this looks good and pragmatic. Two quick clarifications from our side before we lock the pilot: 

1) Will the burst availability (300) be subject to any additional charges beyond the pilot credits in redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf? Put another way, if we spike to the burst cap during a simulated run, will we see billing events?
2) For the streaming pool: are those counted toward the same token billing model or a per-stream unit for rate card purposes?

If you can confirm those two points, we'll route a technical acceptance to our procurement and get the firewall CIDR later today.

Thanks,
Priya

Priya Singh
SRE Manager | Cardinal Labs
priya.singh@cardinallabs.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cardinallabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cardinallabs.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cardinal pilot — concurrency & streaming clarifications

Priya — quick answers inline.

> 1) Will the burst availability (300) be subject to any additional charges beyond the pilot credits in redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf?

Short answer: for the pilot period we will not bill for usage within the burst cap up to 3x for the configured 90s windows — those will be covered by the pilot credits defined in redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf. If you consistently use burst capacity outside the pilot window we'll treat that as overage and flag for a capacity upgrade.

> 2) For the streaming pool: are those counted toward the same token billing model or a per-stream unit for rate card purposes?

Streaming billing uses the same token-based model for generated output; however for pilot rate accounting we also measure concurrent stream sockets as a separate soft resource (the streaming pool allocation) so you won't be charged extra per-stream during the pilot. Post-pilot we can discuss either a per-stream seat or token-only pricing depending on which is more economical for your workload.

Action: I'll open the pilot quota in our infra console and create a time-limited API key for load testing. Neha — I'll post the API key + onboarding doc in the HubSpot deal record and follow up with a short runbook.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
